commitResults.messageBody:
A tutor had nowhere to note what still needed doing for a student or a
lesson, such as calling a parent or preparing a mock paper (user story
31).

Add the task add, task list, task edit, task done and task delete
commands. A task is attached to a student or to a lesson. Task numbers
stay fixed until the next task list, so completing or deleting a task
never renumbers the others. Deleting a task needs confirm.

Keep tasks in step with the data they are about: a task follows its
lesson when the lesson is moved and its student when the student is
edited, and is deleted with either. Deleting a student now counts their
tasks in the confirmation message.

Save tasks in the data file as an optional list, so existing data files
still load. The hw/ and pay/ links are parsed but give the specified
"list first" errors until homework and payments exist.

Update the User Guide and the help command, and add tests.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add lesson repeat and back-dated lessons
commitResults.messageBody:
A tutor could only book lessons one at a time and could not record a
lesson that had already happened (user stories 8 and 9).

Add the lesson repeat command, which books a weekly series (2-52
lessons, 1-12 weeks apart) as all or nothing: the whole series is
checked first and rolled back if adding fails. Every lesson of a series
shares a series id, which is kept when an occurrence is moved or its
status changes, so the series can be found and cancelled together
later. A series is refused for an archived student.

Add the past/ flag to lesson add so that a lesson up to 2 years in the
past can be recorded, and accept today and tmr as dates.

The series id is saved as an optional field, so existing data files
still load. The student's level at booking uses the existing
academicLevel snapshot.

Update the User Guide and the help command, and add tests.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add sort command to order persons by name
commitResults.messageBody:
Persons are listed in the order they were added, so a tutor with many
contacts has no quick way to scan them alphabetically.

Add a sort command that orders all persons by name, ignoring letter
case, in ascending order by default or descending order with the desc
argument. The sorted order is kept in the address book so that it is
saved and shown again on the next launch, and the command shows all
persons so a filtered list does not hide the result.

Add sortPersons to Model, ModelManager, AddressBook and
UniquePersonList to support the command. Add tests for the command,
its parser and the new model methods, and document the command in the
User Guide.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add level, subject, rate and venue value objects
commitResults.messageBody:
TutorFlow needs to record who a student is and what they are taught,
but the address book only has name, phone, email, address and tags
fields, none of which describe a student's level, subjects, rate or
usual venue.

Add Level, Subject, Rate and Venue as validated, immutable value
objects in the same style as the existing Name and Phone classes.
Levels are P1-P6, S1-S5 and J1-J2. Subjects are short free text that is
compared ignoring case. Rates are 0 to 9999.99 dollars with up to two
decimal places. Venues are 1-100 characters of free text.

The classes are not used yet, so behavior is unchanged. They are tested
on their own so that the commit passes the existing checks.

commitResults.messageTitle: Replace address and tags with student details in Person
commitResults.messageBody:
A Person only holds contact details, an address and tags, so TutorFlow
cannot yet record what a tutor needs to know about a student: their
level, the subjects taught, the lesson rate or the usual venue. Teammates
cannot start on lessons, payments or filtering until these exist.

Give Person a level, a set of subjects, a rate and an optional venue,
and make the email optional, as a tutor often only has a phone number.
Remove the address and tags, which nothing else uses, together with the
Address and Tag classes. A single Person class is used rather than a
Student subclass, so that no code needs to cast between the two.

Two persons now count as the same when they share a phone number and a
name that matches ignoring case, instead of the name alone, because
unrelated students can share a name. Optional values are returned as
Optional so that callers cannot forget to handle a missing one.

Update the add and edit commands, the Jackson storage, the sample data
and the person card to match. Existing remark and sort behavior is
unchanged. The tests are updated and extended to cover the new fields.

commitResults.messageBody:

Change the user-facing text of the add, edit, delete, list, find,

messages, to say student. Only the text changes. The constants keep
their names and the behavior is the same.

commitResults.messageBody:

diagram about the alternative design for tags, which no longer exist.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge pull request #39 from joshmode/add-student-fields
Allow common punctuation in student names
commitResults.messageBody:
Names such as "Priya s/o Kumar", "O'Brien-Smith Jr." or
"Tan Wei Ming (twin A)" were rejected because only letters, digits and
spaces were accepted. The feature specification expects names to permit
the punctuation needed to tell students apart, and rejecting real names
is the kind of over-strict validation users trip over.

A name must still start with a letter or digit so that a blank or
punctuation-only name stays invalid.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add lesson date, time, duration and status types
commitResults.messageBody:
A lesson needs validated values for when it happens and how long it
runs. Dates accept ISO (2026-09-22) and d/M/yyyy, times accept 24-hour
and 12-hour forms, and durations are 15 to 480 minutes in steps of 15.
The status distinguishes scheduled, completed, cancelled and missed
lessons so that only scheduled lessons take part in conflict checks.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add Lesson and a unique lesson list
commitResults.messageBody:
A lesson links a student, identified by name and phone number, to a
subject, date, time, duration and optional venue. It rejects a slot
that runs past midnight and reports whether it overlaps another
scheduled lesson on the same date by at least one minute, so that
back-to-back lessons are not flagged.

Person gains hasIdentity so that lessons and persons share a single
definition of who a student is. UniqueLessonList rejects lessons that
share student, subject, date, time and duration.

commitResults.messageTitle: Store lessons in the address book and model
commitResults.messageBody:
The address book now owns a list of lessons next to its persons, and
the model exposes add, delete, replace and conflict lookups plus a
filtered lesson list for the agenda to show.

Lessons belong to a student, so deleting a student also removes their
lessons, and editing the name or phone number of a student keeps their
lessons attached instead of leaving them orphaned.

commitResults.messageTitle: Save and load lessons in the JSON data file
commitResults.messageBody:
Lessons are written next to the students in the data file. A data file
without a lesson list still loads, so files written before lessons
existed keep working. Field conversion in JsonAdaptedLesson shares one
helper that checks presence and validity, so each field is handled the
same way and a bad value reports the matching constraint message.

commitResults.messageTitle: Support rescheduling, cancelling and ordering lessons
commitResults.messageBody:
Moving a lesson keeps its student, subject and status, and cancelling
keeps the whole record with its reason, so a cancelled slot is still
known when a fee is disputed. A lesson can also tell whether it is
still upcoming and format its time range.

The model now shows lessons in agenda order (date, start time, then
student name), so the index a user sees in the agenda is the index the
lesson commands act on. Overlap lookups no longer report a lesson as
overlapping itself, which a reschedule would otherwise trip over.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add parsing helpers for lesson commands
commitResults.messageBody:
The lesson commands share a few argument shapes: dates, times and
durations, a reason for cancelling, flags such as week/ that take no
value, and a check that every required prefix is present. Putting them
in ParserUtil lets each command parser stay a few lines long.

A missing prefix now lists exactly which parameters are missing, so a
tutor typing quickly can see what to add. Flags reject a value, so
"week/yes" is reported instead of being silently accepted.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add the lesson add command
commitResults.messageBody:
"lesson add st/INDEX d/DATE t/TIME" schedules a lesson for a student
in the displayed student list. To keep typing short, the subject can
be left out when the student takes only one, the duration defaults to
60 minutes and the venue defaults to the student's venue.

A subject the student does not take, a past date, a date more than two
years ahead, a lesson that would run past midnight and an exact
duplicate are rejected with a message that says what to fix. An overlap
with another scheduled lesson only warns, because a tutor may double
book on purpose, and back-to-back lessons are not an overlap.

Lesson commands share the "lesson" command word, which a new
LessonCommandParser dispatches to the right parser.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add the lesson list and agenda commands
commitResults.messageBody:
"lesson list st/INDEX" shows a student's upcoming lessons, or all of
them including past and cancelled ones with "all/". "agenda" shows
today's lessons, "agenda d/DATE" a given day and "agenda week/" the
Monday to Sunday week containing the day. Both set the lesson list
that is currently shown, so the number next to a lesson is the index
that the lesson commands take.

The agenda marks lessons that overlap another one, keeps cancelled
lessons visible but leaves them out of the count and total time, and
says so when a day has no lessons instead of failing. A flag such as
"week/yes" that should not take a value is reported.

The shared student lookup moves into LessonCommandUtil so that lesson
add and lesson list use the same index check.

commitResults.messageTitle: Share optional-value parsing between lesson parsers
commitResults.messageBody:
Lesson add and the upcoming lesson move both read several optional
values, each of which was a four-line "if present then parse" block.
ParserUtil.parseOptional returns the parsed value or null, which keeps
each parser short and handles every optional value the same way.

LessonCommandUtil also gains the lesson index lookup and the past-date
check, so that lesson add no longer carries its own copy of the check.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add the lesson move and lesson cancel commands
commitResults.messageBody:
"lesson move INDEX" reschedules the lesson at that index in the lesson
list that is currently shown. Only the given date, time, duration and
venue change, so the tutor does not re-enter the student or subject.
A move that creates an overlap still succeeds with a warning, while a
completed or cancelled lesson, a past or very distant new date, a slot
past midnight and a move onto an identical lesson are rejected.

"lesson cancel INDEX [r/REASON]" keeps the lesson in the agenda marked
as cancelled with its reason, so that the record of the booking is
kept for billing. A cancelled lesson no longer counts as an overlap.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document the lesson commands in the User Guide
commitResults.messageBody:
Describes lesson add, agenda, lesson list, lesson move and lesson cancel
with their formats, defaults, limits and examples, and adds them to the
command summary. The format notes now explain flags such as week/ that
take no value, and use parameters that exist in TutorFlow instead of the
leftover AB3 t/TAG example. The add section states which punctuation a
student name may contain.

design alternatives considered for how a lesson refers to its student
and for what to do when lessons overlap. The model and storage
components and the model class diagram now include lessons, and the
manual testing section gets test cases for the lesson commands.

never trigger the wipe.

commitResults.messageTitle: Route null JSON records through data-file recovery
commitResults.messageBody:
JSON null and null student, lesson or subject entries currently escape
as unchecked exceptions. Startup therefore crashes instead of setting
aside the unreadable data file.

Reject null data at the deserialization boundary using the existing
checked error path. Regression tests confirm that reads report loading
errors and leave the original bytes untouched.

commitResults.messageTitle: Number retained cancellations by their list positions
commitResults.messageBody:
Repeatedly rebooking and cancelling the same slot can leave equal
cancelled records. Looking each record up with indexOf prints the first
record's number for both entries.

Enumerate displayed positions when formatting day and week agendas so
every retained record receives its own usable lesson number.

commitResults.messageTitle: Retain upcoming filters when a lesson list starts empty
commitResults.messageBody:

predicate. Later additions and completions then use an all-status list,
contrary to the requested view.

Install the requested filter before returning the empty-state message.
Cover a later addition and completion through the same active view.

commitResults.messageTitle: Deduplicate Unicode subjects consistently
commitResults.messageBody:
Case-insensitive equality treats dotted and dotless I as equal, but
lowercasing strings produces different hashes. Subject sets can then
retain duplicates and make an omitted lesson subject look ambiguous.

Apply the same per-code-point case folding when computing the hash.
Cover Turkish I variants and Greek sigma variants in real sets.

commitResults.messageTitle: Preserve saved data when a write is interrupted
commitResults.messageBody:
Writing directly to the data file truncates its previous contents
before the new save is complete. A failed write can therefore destroy
the only saved copy while the app reports a recoverable save error.

Write to a sibling temporary file and replace the target atomically
only after all bytes are written. Reject unsupported atomic moves
through the existing save-error path instead of risking the old file.
Cover interrupted writes, replacement, Unicode and temporary cleanup.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use one preview template for student deletion
commitResults.messageBody:
The preview before a student is deleted is built in two places, one
for a student with homework and one for a student without, and the
one for homework gives "and all recorded feedback." with no advice
to archive. The specification asks for the counts of what is
deleted and the advice to archive instead whenever there is
homework.

Let's build the preview and the success message from one
description of the records that are deleted. A student with
homework gets the number of items, including the upcoming ones, and
the advice to archive. Feedback is not part of the template, so a
sentence about it is added only when there is some.

commitResults.messageTitle: Give each help entry parameters and an example
commitResults.messageBody:
help COMMAND prints the usage of a command, but the commands that
the alpha adds (hw, archive, restore, demo and lesson prep) print
one line only, and the descriptions of list and today say how those
commands worked before the alpha.

The usage strings also appear in error messages, so they must not
change. Let's give those commands a second block with the
parameters and an example, which help prints after the usage, and
bring the descriptions of list and today up to date.

HelpCommandTest requires an example for every command that help
lists, so a new command cannot be listed with a bare usage line.

commitResults.messageTitle: Link the Command Summary menu entry to its section
commitResults.messageBody:
The site menu lists "Command Summary" under the User Guide, but its
link ends in #faq, so a reader who picks it lands on the FAQ.

Let's point the link at #command-summary, the anchor of the heading
that the entry names.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show the unsupported data version in a window
commitResults.messageBody:
When the data file comes from a newer version, TutorFlow stops at
start-up by throwing out of init(). JavaFX prints the stack trace on
the console and opens no window, so a user who starts the JAR from a
file manager sees nothing happen and cannot tell that the data file is
the reason.

Let's record the refusal in init() instead of throwing it, and show
its message in an error dialog from start() before exiting with
status 1. The data file stays untouched. stop() returns early when
there is no model, since JavaFX still calls it after the refusal.

commitResults.messageTitle: Parse archive and restore with their own parser
commitResults.messageBody:
archive and restore read their index in AddressBookParser, and an
invalid index gets "Index must be a positive integer." Every other
command that takes an index answers Invalid command format! followed
by its usage, which is what the specification asks for.

Let's add ArchiveCommandParser, which reports a bad index with the
usage of archive or of restore. It uses new ParserUtil helpers that
other parsers can reuse: parseIndex with a usage, invalidFormat and
requirePrefixesFound.

ArchiveCommand gets usage and message constants, null checks, equals,
hashCode and toString, and the help entries share the usage constants.

commitResults.messageTitle: Report malformed list arguments as invalid format
commitResults.messageBody:
list answers text such as "list foo" with the long usage text alone,
and a flag with a value such as "archived/yes" the same way. The
specification asks for Invalid command format! followed by the usage,
and every other flag in the application says that it takes no value.

Let's report text before the prefixes with Invalid command format!
and the usage, and a value after archived/ or all/ with the flag
message. Giving both flags keeps the usage alone, as the
specification says for list.

ListCommand also gets equals, hashCode and toString, and its flags are
named isArchivedOnly and isArchivedIncluded to read as booleans.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use the note of add when an edit repeats a name
commitResults.messageBody:
Adding a student whose name is taken says "Note: you already have a
student named X." Editing a student to a taken name says "another
student", although the specification asks for the same note in both.

Let's share the text of the note between add and edit, and add a test
that fixes the wording.

commitResults.messageTitle: Rename the archive and stored flags as booleans
commitResults.messageBody:
Person and JsonAdaptedPerson name their archive flag "archived", and
Name, Phone, Email and Venue name a constructor flag "stored". The
Java coding standard asks for names such as isArchived, so that
linters can verify them.

Let's rename them. The key in the data file stays "archived" through
an explicit @JsonProperty, because renaming the field would otherwise
change the file format. ArchivedStudentStorageTest guards the key, and
PersonBuilder can build an archived student.

commitResults.messageTitle: Give student commands matching hash codes
commitResults.messageBody:
AddCommand, DeleteCommand, EditCommand and its descriptor, FindCommand,
RemarkCommand, SortCommand and ViewCommand override equals without
hashCode, so two equal commands can hash differently. The predicate of
find has the same gap.

Let's add hashCode from the fields that equals compares, and a test
that equal commands also have equal hash codes.

commitResults.messageTitle: Read s/o in a name as text instead of a subject
commitResults.messageBody:
A name that contains s/o, such as Priya s/o Kumar, is cut at s/
because that is the prefix of a subject. The tutor gets a student
called Priya with the subject "o Kumar". The specification lists this
as a known limitation and asks users to write d/o or "son of",
although s/o is the usual form.

Let's hide a stand-alone s/o from the tokenizer in add and edit, and
write it out again in the name and the venue. A word that only starts
with s/o, such as s/oxygen, is still a subject. A subject that is the
single lower-case letter o can no longer be typed as s/o.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test that find returns archived students
commitResults.messageBody:
The specification says that find reaches any student whose name
contains the keyword, and it does not exclude archived students. A
tutor needs this to find an archived student before restoring them,
but no test records the behavior.

Let's add one, so that a change to the filter of find cannot hide
archived students without a failing test.

commitResults.messageTitle: Compare homework descriptions ignoring letter case
commitResults.messageBody:
Two assignments for the same student and due date count as duplicates
only when their descriptions match letter for letter, so "algebra
q1-10" is accepted beside "Algebra Q1-10". That is the double entry
that the duplicate rule exists to stop.

Let's compare the descriptions ignoring letter case. They are already
trimmed and have repeated spaces collapsed. The rejection names the
homework that is already recorded, with its own capitalization.

HomeworkTest and AddressBookHomeworkTest cover the rule, the identity
checks and the link to the student.

commitResults.messageTitle: Name the bad field when homework fails to load
commitResults.messageBody:
A homework item with a missing or invalid field is rejected with
"Invalid homework: null" or the text of a Java exception, so a tutor
who edited the data file by hand cannot tell which field is wrong. The
status is also read letter for letter, so "submitted" in lower case
invalidates the whole file although the file is meant to be editable.

Let's check each field and report the one that is wrong by name. The
status is read in any letter case through HomeworkStatus.fromText,
which the parser can share. The file still writes the upper-case name,
so its format does not change.

commitResults.messageTitle: Report homework results in the spec wording
commitResults.messageBody:
Homework commands build their messages inline, so the wording has
drifted from the spec and no test can name a message. The delete
prompt omits "Nothing is deleted.", a backward status move omits
"Feedback already recorded is kept.", list rows separate columns
with two spaces, and an empty history shows a headline the spec
does not give.

Let's follow the spec wording, keep each message in a constant of
its command and give every command a null check, equals, hashCode
and toString. The new tests pin the exact output of each command.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject malformed homework commands as specified
commitResults.messageBody:
Homework commands answer a missing prefix, a bad index or a flag
given a value with ad hoc text. A bare "hw status 1" says nothing
about s/, an index that is not a number gives the generic index
message, and the sub-command list is built inline.

Let's name each missing prefix, show the invalid-format line and
the usage string for a bad index, and answer a flag that is given
a value with the usage string. The usage string of hw status
follows the spec.

commitResults.messageTitle: Report unsaved changes when a save fails
commitResults.messageBody:
A command whose write to disk fails ends with the reason and the
advice to fix it, but not with the line that tells the user how to
retry. The spec ends every failed save with the unsaved-changes
line, and a failure without a message reports "null" as its reason.

Let's append the line to the failed result and name the kind of
failure when the exception has no message. The new tests cover a
full disk, an unwritable file, a failure without a message, the
save command, and commands that only show information.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test the start-up messages for the data file
commitResults.messageBody:
The start-up messages for a first run, an unreadable data file and
a data file from a newer version are only checked in part. Nothing
tests that deleting the data file starts empty again, or that a
second unreadable file is numbered rather than replacing the first.

Let's test the exact text of each start-up message and the files
that remain on disk.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test the supported data schema versions
commitResults.messageBody:
The range of schema versions that TutorFlow opens is checked only
through the files of other tests. A version just outside the range
or a version that is not a whole number could slip through.

Let's test the edges of the range, an absent version, a version
that is not a whole number and the refusal text.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test that the log holds no personal details
commitResults.messageBody:
The requirements keep contact details, fees and notes out of the
log files, but no test checks it. A log call that includes a
value typed by the user would pass unnoticed.

Let's capture every log record at every level while commands run
and fail the test if one holds a distinctive name, phone number,
email, venue, fee, remark, homework or feedback.

commitResults.messageTitle: Require every address book view to list homework
commitResults.messageBody:
ReadOnlyAddressBook gives a default empty list of homework, so a
class that implements it and forgets to override the method is saved
and copied without its homework, and nothing fails. The default only
served implementations from before homework existed, and the only
two are AddressBook and a test stub.

Let's make getHomeworkList abstract like the lists of students and
lessons, so that the compiler finds a view that leaves it out. A test
checks that resetData takes the homework from any implementation.

commitResults.messageTitle: Never set aside a data file that cannot be opened
commitResults.messageBody:
A data file that another program holds, or that the permissions
forbid reading, fails to load like a damaged one, so TutorFlow
renames it to .corrupt and starts empty. At the first start of a new
version this renames the older file, which may be valid, and the
students in it are never migrated. The file is also renamed on the
next save when the rename failed at start-up.

Let's tell a file that cannot be opened from one whose content is
invalid. Only invalid content is set aside. For a file that cannot be
opened, TutorFlow does not start: a window names the file and the
reason, nothing is renamed or written over it, and the next start that
can open it loads or migrates it. A null document is invalid content,
and the storage refuses to save over a file that was not opened.

Report the lesson status before the billing refusal in move and cancel
commitResults.messageBody:
Completing a lesson always records a charge, so every completed lesson
was refused with "Cannot change a billed lesson" and the specified
"Cannot reschedule a completed lesson" and "Cannot cancel a completed
lesson" messages could not be reached for it. A missed lesson that was
billed, or a cancelled one, was affected the same way.

Check the status first in lesson move and lesson cancel and only then
the charge. The existing tests expected the wrong message for a
completed lesson, so they now cover a completed, a missed and a
scheduled lesson that has a charge.

commitResults.messageTitle: Collapse repeated spaces in a student's remark
commitResults.messageBody:
The specification (3.2) says that runs of two or more spaces inside a
value collapse to one and that surrounding whitespace is trimmed, and
every other free-text value does this. A remark was stored exactly as
typed, so "remark 1 r/Likes   swimming" kept all three spaces.

Normalise the remark in its constructor, as Venue and Name do.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use the specified wording for the delete confirmation prompts
commitResults.messageBody:

hw delete (4.25) asks "This deletes homework '...', any feedback, and N
linked task(s). Type 'hw delete N confirm' to proceed." whenever tasks
are linked. It printed two other sentences, one for tasks alone and one
for tasks with feedback. Use the specified sentence for both.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract shared parsing helpers out of the command parsers
commitResults.messageBody:
Several parsers carried their own copy of the same logic, so a fix to
one left the others behind.

- CommandInput and SubCommandParser replace the command word regex and
  switch that LessonCommandParser and TaskCommandParser each had, and
  the regex in AddressBookParser.
- ConfirmableIndex replaces the index-and-confirm parsing copied in
  DeleteCommandParser, TaskDeleteCommandParser and HomeworkCommandParser.
- DemoCommandParser takes the demo argument check out of
  AddressBookParser, which now only reads the command word.
- HomeworkCommandParser uses the prefixes in CliSyntax instead of its
  own copies, and AddressBookParser reuses ParserUtil.requirePrintable.

Parsing behaviour and error messages are unchanged.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test that the three delete commands strip Unicode whitespace alike

strips surrounding whitespace with String.strip(). Section 3.2 says
leading and trailing whitespace is trimmed and makes no exception for

Note it in the Developer Guide.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show reversals correctly in the account statement
commitResults.messageBody:
AccountStatement treated every entry that was not a CHARGE as a payment,
so after pay reverse the running balance went down instead of up and the
totals counted the reversal as a further payment. balance then disagreed
with dues.

Use kind().increasesBalance() for the running balance, take charge and
payment reversals out of the charged and paid totals, and describe them
as "reversal of charge|payment (DATE) $X.XX" as section 4.29 does. Add
tests for a reversed payment (the 4.29 example) and a reversed charge.

commitResults.messageTitle: Read dates written in more ways
commitResults.messageBody:
A date can now be written day first or year first, with / - . or a space
between the parts, with the month as a number or an English name, and with a
two-digit year. FlexibleDateParser reads them. A date that can be read both ways
takes the reading nearer to today, and the day first if they are equally near.
Dates in the data file stay YYYY-MM-DD.

depth failure into DataLoadingException so startup uses the safe
recovery path. Add a regression test for malicious nesting.

commitResults.messageTitle: Link tasks to payments
commitResults.messageBody:
Tasks can currently point only at a student, a lesson or a
homework item. Specification 4.31 also allows a payment link.

Let's add an optional payment UUID to Task, keep the existing
lesson/homework exclusivity, and display the linked payment in task
lists. The link is by UUID so reversing or editing a payment does not
change what the task is about.

commitResults.messageTitle: Support pay/INDEX in task add
commitResults.messageBody:
The task add command still rejects every payment link because there
is no numbered payment list to resolve.

Let's resolve pay/INDEX against the snapshot from the last pay list,
re-find the payment by UUID, and derive its student. Missing or
out-of-range indices and deleted payments now use the failure messages
in specification 4.31.

commitResults.messageTitle: Persist task payment links
commitResults.messageBody:
A task payment link is lost on restart unless it has a storage
field and a schema version that protects it.

Let's save paymentId in each task, advance the schema to 18, and skip
stale tasks whose payment is missing or belongs to another student.
Tests cover round trips, older-schema refusal, and a payment task
surviving a reversal.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document payment links for tasks
commitResults.messageBody:
The guides still say that pay/INDEX is only a reserved format and
leave the payment-link storage migration undocumented.

Let's describe how to link a task to a listed payment, the failure
messages, the schema 18 protection, and the updated follow-up task
model. This also removes the obsolete integration follow-up line.

commitResults.messageTitle: Bound large input and results
commitResults.messageBody:
A payment accepted an unlimited digit string, and a dense day or
week could render hundreds of kilobytes into the result box.

Limit payments and manual charges to one million dollars, cap
each rendered lesson section at 200 rows, and keep the complete
counts in the headings. The truncation line says how many rows
were omitted. Update the guide and tests for both bounds.

commitResults.messageTitle: Clarify unknown charge subcommands
commitResults.messageBody:
An unknown alphabetic charge form looked like a malformed lesson
index, so users saw a generic format error instead of the two
accepted forms.

Return the charge usage when the first word is not reverse, while
keeping bare numeric and prefix errors unchanged.

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep amounts currency-neutral
commitResults.messageBody:
The SGD-specific payment ceiling assumed one currency, while the
target audience is not scoped to Singapore. Remove the ceiling from
payments and manual charges and restore the existing large-payment
warning.

Keep the 200-row result cap, and add direct tests that headings
retain complete totals while the rows are truncated.

commitResults.messageTitle: Limit payment and homework listings
commitResults.messageBody:
Dense payment and homework histories still rendered every row into
the result box, even though lesson listings were already capped.

Show the first 200 rows and then a Showing N of M line. Keep the
complete numbered selection so pay reverse and indexed homework
commands can still address hidden rows. Document both limits and
add tests that retain every displayed index.

commitResults.messageTitle: Bound travel warnings in agenda output
commitResults.messageBody:
Capping lesson rows did not cap the travel warnings appended
after them, so a dense week could still produce an oversized
result.

Let's limit each rendered summary to 50 travel warnings and show
an N-of-M notice when more exist. Update the guide and add a
regression test.

commitResults.messageTitle: Correct the travel warning count
commitResults.messageBody:
The N-of-M notice counted the newline that prefixes each
warning, so it reported one more warning than it rendered.

Let's count the matching gaps directly and strengthen the test
to assert both the exact shown count and the total.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject misplaced phone separators
commitResults.messageBody:
Phone input accepted trailing and repeated separators because they
were removed before the digit count was checked.

Let's require separators only between non-empty digit groups while
keeping the old stored-data reader permissive so existing records
still load.

commitResults.messageTitle: Format rates with a fixed locale
commitResults.messageBody:
Rate display used the system locale, so a comma-decimal locale
rendered $50,00 while the ledger and User Guide use a period.

Let's format rates with Locale.ROOT and cover a comma-decimal default
locale in the test.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add credit withdrawals
commitResults.messageBody:
Students can accumulate credit but had no way to withdraw it, so
an overpayment could only be corrected by changing payment history.

Let's record a withdrawal as a new append-only ledger entry, reject
amounts above available credit, and show it in balances and account
statements. Advance the schema to 18 so older builds do not discard
the new ledger kind.

Document the command and cover persistence, parser failures, full
credit, insufficient credit, future dates and dues allocation.

commitResults.messageTitle: Clarify withdrawal accounting totals
commitResults.messageBody:
Account statements folded withdrawals into the amount paid,
which misstated how much a student had actually paid. Dues also
needed an explicit regression for withdrawals included in the
net-credit allocation.

Let's report paid and withdrawn totals separately, update the
guide, and cover withdrawal-aware FIFO allocation and the remaining
phone-validation branches.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add command-assisted student card actions
commitResults.messageBody:
Student cards show edit, archive and delete controls only when the user hovers, focuses or taps a card. Field editing then fills the command box with existing edit syntax without executing anything or mutating the model.

Keep one shared CommandAssist to own generated drafts and edit-mode cleanup. Clear changed numbered drafts when the list changes, preserve unrelated user input, and expose add n/ from the top toolbar so the CLI remains the single source of truth.

commitResults.messageTitle: Clarify how to list archived students
commitResults.messageBody: The archive usage string only says archive INDEX, so users have to discover the listing flags elsewhere. Mention list archived/ and list all/ in the command's own help and cover the wording with a regression test.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document student card shortcuts
commitResults.messageBody: The new GUI controls and their command-box state rules need to be discoverable in the User Guide and testable by hand. Add the shortcut workflow, draft replacement and cancellation rules, stale-number handling and touch and keyboard access, then give testers matching manual checks.

commitResults.messageTitle: Track generated edit drafts by card
commitResults.messageBody:
Opening card-level edit mode did not own a field draft, so cancel could clear an older shortcut still in the command box. Keep field-draft ownership separate from edit mode and clear only a draft generated by that card's field control.

Cover the older-draft case so newer archive and add shortcuts remain untouched.

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep card actions visible during field editing
commitResults.messageBody:
Keyboard focus moves from a card action into a field-edit control, which hid the card-level archive and delete actions mid-interaction. Treat edit mode as a reason to keep those controls visible until the interaction ends.

Also cover edit-mode cleanup on cancel, replacement and successful command execution.

commitResults.messageTitle: Close edit mode when another card is opened
commitResults.messageBody:
Each card registered its own edit-mode callback, but opening the second card replaced the callback before the first could be closed. Keep the current callback until it has run so only one card can be in field-editing mode at a time.

Add a visible focus outline to the focusable card and cover cross-card editing and displayed-list changes.

commitResults.messageTitle: Refine card and command clearing controls
commitResults.messageBody:
Move the subject pencil into the subject flow so it sits directly after the last subject, and place Cancel beside the card-level edit control where the active edit mode is visible.

Add a clear control to the command box that appears only while text is present, then clears the draft and returns focus. Cover both controls and document the changed layout.

commitResults.messageTitle: Capitalize subjects entered through commands
commitResults.messageBody:
Subjects entered in lower case were stored exactly as typed, so otherwise identical subjects could appear with inconsistent capitalization. Capitalize the first Unicode letter in ParserUtil, which handles add, edit, lesson and filter input in one place.

Use Locale.ROOT casing and revalidate the capitalized value so an unusual Unicode expansion remains a valid subject. Keep stored data untouched for backward compatibility, and document the behavior.

commitResults.messageTitle: Correct subject capitalization documentation
commitResults.messageBody: The model documentation still said subject case was always preserved, and the developer guide described the uppercase helper inaccurately. Clarify that command input is capitalized on entry while stored data keeps its original case.

commitResults.messageTitle: Address finance review feedback
commitResults.messageBody:
Implicit billing, orphaned lesson references and repeated ledger scans
make financial behavior harder to reuse and saved data less reliable.
Payment syntax and messages also differ from the alpha specification.

Make completion and charging an explicit atomic model operation that
returns the charge. Refuse deletion of billed lessons, validate ledger
snapshots in bulk, and cache the immutable ledger view.

Support pay with amt/, optional dates and notes, while preserving the
earlier payment/a syntax as an alias. Name missing JSON fields, correct
dues wording, and recommend archiving in deletion previews.

Inject clocks for deterministic finance workflows and add regressions
for billed-lesson persistence, large ledger copies and dated payments.
Document the balance-summary scope and deferred account statements.
